_comment.DisableClusterFlattening: Set to true to stop ironing the terrain under a city flat and let the streets
follow it instead. Cities become genuinely three dimensional.
This is now the DEFAULT. Set it to false to get the old ironed-flat city back;
that path still exists and is still tested, but it is no longer what ships.
Streets, traffic, pedestrians, the player's car, the pavements, the ground under
them, buildings, shops, quest markers, the intercity tram and the starting coins
all follow the terrain. The nine defects reported from play on 2026-08-30 are
cleared, each measured rather than argued.
Still open, and deliberately so: what an intercity line IS - a graded embankment,
a viaduct on pylons, or a deliberately elevated line - is a design decision that
has not been made, so the track is still a flat ribbon with no geometry drawn.
Terrain still buries block interiors (18-25 % of block area, median 2.3 m),
which needs a finer in-city elevation grid than one sample per 20 m. And about
half the citizen loop walker's waypoints land on or outside their own kerb.
